Describe common medical conditions and examine cultural and linguistic implications.
Exhibit intercultural communication skills in managing diverse interactions and power dynamics.
Employ the six-steps ethical decision-making process to solve ethical dilemmas.
Apply proper skills in using various interpreting modalities.

rows.title: Professional Skills for Healthcare Interpreters
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe challenges in special populations and explain strategies to promote health equity.
Articulate language access laws, regulations, and accreditation standards.
Analyze job opportunities and self-assess readiness.

rows.title: Family Systems
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the effectiveness of wellness and recovery best practices and interventions with families in behavioral health settings.
Produce service delivery documentation based on behavioral health standards.
Evaluate the impact of self-awareness when working with families.

rows.title: How Trauma Affects Our Lives
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze common causes of and responses to trauma.
Identify common approaches and local resources for promoting recovery from trauma.

rows.title: Elder Abuse Prevention
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the risk factors and indicators of elder abuse, neglect, and exploitation.
Explain legal and ethical duties to report abuse and services available.

rows.title: Mindful Stress Reduction
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate mindfulness practices for personal stress reduction
Select and practice appropriate stress reduction techniques

rows.title: Transgender Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define key concepts and terminology, and access reliable research and resources, related to transgender and nonbinary communities.
Assess the health status, health needs and health inequities of transgender and nonbinary communities.
Apply trans-inclusive concepts and skills for working with transgender and nonbinary clients and communities.

rows.title: Treatment Modalities in Addiction Recovery
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the Diagnostic Statistical Manual (DSM)-5 criteria for and the various treatment models used in substance use and co-occurring disorder treatment.
Asses and integrate stages of change theory, fluctuating motivation and resistance within treatment planning and intervention.
Examine and demonstrate competency in multidimensinal assessment and case conceptionalization to develop appropriate treatment plans for clients with substance use disorders.
Apply evidence-based treatment strategies, their benefits and challenges within the continuum of care to support recovery and relapse prevention in a range of treatment settings.
Integrate culturally responsive and client-centered approaches to ensure ethical and personalized treatment planning for diverse populations in treatment counseling.

rows.title: Music, Art, and Literature: Traditional
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify traditional artistic figures before the nineteenth century and basic aesthetic characteristics.
Combine a formal understanding of aesthetics with a personal reaction to the arts to enable an informed response to artistic expression.
Analyze works of art in their historical and cultural contexts through discussion and writing.
Evaluate the influence of non-Western cultures on Western artistic movements as well as the ways in which the idea of a Western canon was constructed.

rows.title: Bay Area Arts
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify artists who have left their mark on the Bay Area's cultural landscape as well as the aesthetic characteristics of their work.
Analyze artists' works in the context of Bay Area history.
Distinguish among the artistic contributions of various regions of the Bay Area and San Francisco neighborhoods.
Apply an intercultural appreciation of aesthetics to the study of Bay Area artworks.

rows.title: African-American Music, Art and Literature
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify elements of the African and African-American aesthetic in modern American music, sculpture, paintings, architecture, and literature.
Summarize the major contributions of the African-American canon of artistic expression.
Analyze texts by and concerning African-American authors for their cultural and historical context through discussion and writing.
Describe the blending of African and European cultures that creates a unique African-American expression in several artistic genres.

rows.title: Philosophies of Religion
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify core concepts of the course's religions as represented in their sacred texts.
Compare the world views shown in sacred texts.
Analyze sacred texts.

rows.title: Human Sexuality
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate current and historical methodologies used to study human sexuality, including physiological, biological, and anatomical aspects of sexuality, as well as relevant cultural values.
Compare the anatomical, physiological, and psychological stages of development across the life span.

Identify the full spectrum of sexual expression, including auto-erotic behavior, lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning, intersex and asexual (LGBTQQIA+), as well as sex among the disabled, young, and elderly.
Evaluate the biological, social, and psychological issues associated with conception, pregnancy and birth, including reproductive justice.
Evaluate relevant health information, including healthy relationships, sexual dysfunction, sexually transmitted infections, and commercial sex.

rows.title: Islam: Identity & Culture
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the origins, foundational principles and practices of Islam with those of other major religions.
Evaluate major differences among historical and current Muslim groups, including American Muslims.
Analyze gender equity and disparity in Muslim texts.
Assess the scientific and cultural contributions of Muslims.
Analyze representations of Islam and Muslims in the media and popular culture.

rows.title: Demystifying the Middle East
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the diverse identities of people of the Middle East in their geographic, historical, and political context.
Assess power dynamics and challenge stereotypes related to the Middle East.
Apply methods of inquiry from the social sciences and humanities to critique Orientalism and explore alternatives.
Analyze activist, feminist, and aesthetic movements in the Middle East, including their major creative expressions.
Explain the importance of major cultural, artistic, and intellectual contributions from the Middle East and the diaspora.

rows.title: Women and Gender in the Middle East
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the impact of religious and cultural gender norms in relation to women’s lives in the Middle East/SWANA.
Assess the diversity of Middle Eastern/SWANA women's experience in relation to social, historical, and geographical context.
Evaluate Western perspectives on Middle Eastern/SWANA women historically and currently.
Compare political and social movements in the SWANA/Middle East region as relates to gender issues over time using social science methodologies.
Analyze contributions that SWANA/Middle Eastern women have made in artistic and intellectual production.

rows.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze race as a social construct and the changing definitions of race.

Examine the impact and histories of immigration, colonization, and diaspora in the shaping of ethnic and racial formations in the United States, including Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and Latinx Americans.
Assess historical roots and contemporary consequences of prejudice, discrimination, and institutional racism.

Describe and evaluate major theories of race and ethnicity, and how the intersections of social class, gender, sexuality, and ability pervade racial and ethnic identity formations in the United States.
Analyze representations in the popular press and other media that influence relations in ethnic and racial groups in American society.
Appraise and create artistic and cultural representations that speak to race and ethnicity in the United States.
Identify and evaluate social movements and/or policy debates for racial justice and equity.

rows.title: Pacific Islanders in the United States
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the diversity of the Pacific Islander and Oceania communities in the United States and beyond.
Implement indigenous research methodologies used in the study of peoples from the Pacific Islands and Oceania.
Examine the impact and histories of immigration, migration, colonization, and diaspora in the shaping of Pacific Islander & Oceania ethnic and racial formations in the United States.
Appraise and create Pacific Islander and Oceania artistic and cultural representations that speak to race and ethnicity in the United States.
Analyze the relationship between culture, power, knowledge, and decolonization in shaping Pacific Islander identities.

rows.title: Trauma and the Arts: An Interdisciplinary Approach
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate works of art across disciplines as to how they respond to historical traumatic events.
Analyze visual art and public monuments in the context of historical events and cultural memory.
Compare literary works, including personal testimony, in terms of figurative language and themes related to the ongoing effects of trauma.
Identify the function of music and dance in bearing witness, cultural resilience, and sustaining community.
Identify and analyze activist artistic responses to personal and political oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Sexism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze sexism as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes in relation to sexism.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action against sexism.
Explain the intersectionality of sexism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Ableism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze ableism as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes regarding ableism.
Examine individual and collective ways to take action in response to ableism.
Explain the intersectionality of ableism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Transphobia
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze transphobia as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes regarding transphobia.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action against transphobia.
Explain the intersectionality of transphobia with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Antisemitism/Anti-Arabism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze antisemitism and anti-Arabism as systems of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes regarding antisemitism and anti-Arabism.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action in response to antisemitism and anti-Arabism.
Explain the intersectionality of distinct forms of antisemitism and anti-Arabism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Interior Design Studio I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create interior design solutions in response to programming, space planning and circulation
Evaluate a proposed interiors solution against project requirements
Analyze and communicate design process visually, orally, in writing, and in models (hand and digital)
Research and select appropriate materials and specifications for function and aesthetic values

rows.title: Elementary Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally using present and past tense syntax at a beginning level in Italian.
Read and write in Italian at a beginning level.
Apply clear Italian pronunciation and intonation when responding to spoken Italian at a beginning level.
Explain elements of Italian culture at a level appropriate for a beginning-level Italian language learner.

rows.title: Beginning Conversational Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intelligible pronunciation and intonation at an intermediate-low level when narrating in the present or past
Communicate using accurate grammatical structures in Italian at intermediate-low level to describe daily routines, reciprocal actions, and speak about past events

Respond effectively to spoken Italian with appropriate grammatical forms, accurate vocabulary, and clear pronunciation at an intermediate-low level demonstrating an understanding of human interactions
Compare aspects of Italian culture and geography related to fashion, cuisine, technology, and regions

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Conversational Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in intermediate-high level spoken conversations in Italian using correct pronunciation, grammar, and syntax.
Apply intermediate-high level skills in listening comprehension.
Explain elements of the history, culture and social trends of the Italian-speaking world.

rows.title: Elementary Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally using present and past tense syntax at a beginning level in Italian.
Read and write in Italian at a beginning level.
Apply clear Italian pronunciation and intonation when responding to spoken Italian at a beginning level.
Explain elements of Italian culture at a level appropriate for a beginning-level Italian language learner.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Read and write in Italian at a near-elementary level.
Communicate orally with correct syntax using the present perfect and imperfect, and the future indicative tenses at a near-elementary level in Italian.
Apply clear Italian pronunciation and intonation when responding to spoken Italian at an elementary level.
Explain and compare elements of Italian culture and society at a near-elementary level.

rows.title: Intermediate Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Italian at an intermediate level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and clear intonation.
Interpret the main idea of a written text in Italian at an intermediate level.
Analyze and compose short written communications in Italian at an intermediate level.
Assess and articulate aspects of Italian culture responsively at an intermediate level.

rows.title: Elementary Japanese
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Japanese at a basic beginning level.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a basic beginning level.
Apply a cultural understanding of Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a basic beginning level when composing short communications.
Describe basic elements of Japanese culture in relation to diverse communication practices.

rows.title: Continuation of Beginning Conversational Japanese
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at an advanced beginning level in Japanese
Explain elements of Japanese culture at an advanced beginning level

rows.title: Beginning Kanji for Reading and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify simple words and phrases using appropriate kanji characters at the beginning level.
Comprehend reading materials at the beginning level.
Compose paragraphs using appropriate kanji characters at the beginning level.

rows.title: Intermediate Kanji for Reading and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Comprehend the meaning of approximately 200 single characters at an intermediate level and apply that knowledge to the meaning of compound characters
Identify pronunciation of kanji with phonetic elements at an intermediate level
Identify and interpret kanji’s root meaning based on radicals at an intermediate level
Analyze authentic reading materials that contain kanji at an intermediate level
Compose short essays by selecting appropriate kanji at an intermediate level

rows.title: Elementary Japanese Part II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Japanese at a basic beginning level.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a basic beginning level.
Apply a cultural understanding of Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a basic beginning level when composing short communications
Describe basic elements of Japanese culture in relation to diverse communication practices.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Japanese Part I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Japanese at a pre-advanced beginning level.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a pre-advanced beginning level.
Compose short communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a pre-advanced beginning level.
Explain basic elements of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Intermediate Japanese
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at a basic intermediate level in Japanese.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a basic intermediate level.
Compose short communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a basic intermediate level.
Discuss various aspects of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Intermediate Japanese Part I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at a pre-basic intermediate level in Japanese.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a pre-basic intermediate level.
Compose short communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a pre-basic intermediate level.
Discuss essential elements of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Japanese
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at a mid-Intermediate level in Japanese.
Analyze the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a mid-intermediate level.
Create written communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a mid-intermediate level.
Evaluate elements of Japanese culture in relation to diverse communication practices

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Japanese Part II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Japanese at a mid-intermediate level.
Analyze the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a mid intermediate level.
Create written communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a mid-intermediate level.
Evaluate elements of Japanese culture in relation to diverse communication practices.

rows.title: News Reporting and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the characteristics of a good journalist.
Apply the principles and practices of reporting and writing in the production of a news story.
Evaluate the newsworthiness of a story idea by reviewing varying news stories found in a newspaper.
Interpret the ethics and legal rights of a journalist.

rows.title: Copy Editing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and assess the characteristics of a good copy editor.
Use accepted Associated Press style.
Summarize the key ingredients of a news and feature story.
Identify and correct English language usage errors.
Produce headlines suitable for publication in a mass-circulated newspaper, magazine, or news website.

rows.title: News Production and Publication II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify journalistic standards and expectations for a news publication at an advanced beginner level
Describe the editorial and operational structure of a campus news publication at an advanced beginner level
Evaluate whether the campus publication meets the information needs of its audience with an advanced beginner level of understanding
Apply advanced-beginner research and writing skills to develop a portfolio of published works for employment opportunities in the field of journalism

rows.title: Introduction to Magazine Editing and Production
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the various types of writing, editing, photography, illustration and/or design that go into producing a magazine.
Create written, photographic, illustration or design content for a magazine at an introductory level.
Identify and summarize the basic principles and practices that go into producing a magazine.

rows.title: Data and Multimedia Journalism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assemble data, text, and imagery for an infographic
Assess the quality of a data set for use in a journalistic article
Apply the basic principles and practices involved in composing an infographic

rows.title: Introduction to Photojournalism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Collaborate with department editors to organize photographic assignments.
Create aesthetically appealing compositions using various creative tools and camera techniques.
Integrate photographic skills using digital editing techniques and related computer programs and equipment.
Apply skills to create and maintain a portfolio of photojournalism images.
Explain the role of the photojournalist and their work in the field of journalism.

rows.title: The Latinx Experience in the United States
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret the demographic diversity represented by the terms Latinx/Hispanic through analysis of Latinx produced theory and knowledge.

Assess the impact of U.S. expansionism in the 19th Century and the integration of Latinx populations in the U.S. Southwest and Puerto Rico, accounting for issues of colonialism, race and racism, racialization, ethnicity, equity, ethno-centrism, white supremacy, self-determination, liberation, sovereignty, and anti-racism.
Evaluate the intersectionality of race and racism in relation to U.S. government immigration policies and how they impact immigrants from Latin America to the U.S.

Debate the impact of Latinxs on U.S. institutions and society during the Civil Rights and Post Civil Rights eras, specifically reviewing acts of resistance and racial and social justice movements in Latinx communities.

Compare selected aspects of the Latinx experience in the United States related to patterns of assimilation and migrant transnationalism, identifying issues such as multiculturalism and language and education policies.
Critique the Latinx community's cultural contributions to the U.S. and their impact on popular culture and as forms of protest that have encouraged agency and equity.

rows.title: Drug Wars in the Americas
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish the historical and political context that led to the emergence of licit and illicit drugs in the United States and Latin America.
Compare past and present drug reduction and control policies implemented in the war against drugs.
Assess the impact of the United States' political, social, and economic influence in shaping drug laws and drug policy initiatives in Latin America.
Evaluate the impact of the drug wars on democracy, rule of law and civil society in Latin America and the United States.
Appraise the complexity of organized crime, insurgency and terrorism in Latin America and their reliance on the production and sale of illicit drugs to the United States.

rows.title: Diego Rivera: Art and Social Change in Latin America
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the political impact of the Mexican Revolution on artists and the development of public art in Mexico.
Evaluate Diego Rivera's political, cultural and artistic influences.
Analyze and consider the roles and meanings of politically-oriented Latinx art in the San Francisco Bay Area.
Assess the impact of modern political revolutions on Latin American culture.
Compare key cultural figures that carry on Diego Rivera's legacy.

rows.title: Critical Thinking in Latinx Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply theory and knowledge produced by Latinxs and other people of color to critique rhetorical works focused on Latinxs.
Assess U.S. media and popular culture texts for their use of common narratives, stereotypes, or tropes regarding Latinxs, and juxtapose these with Latin American media.
Analyze and interpret the roles that racialization, ethnicity, and white supremacy play in aspects of Latinx experience as represented in popular discourses in the U.S.

Analyze critically through written works the intersection of race and racism as applied to dimensions of difference common to Latinxs in the U.S., including class, national origins, and immigration status.

rows.title: Individual Study in Latin American and Latino/a Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze a research topic or issue in Latin American and Latino/a Studies.
Present an argument that compares similarities and differences among perspectives in Latin American and Latino/a literature.
Synthesize theories and concepts that explain a chosen topic or issue in Latin American and Latino/a Studies.

rows.title: Shaping Public Policy for Labor and Community Organizations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the role of powerful individuals and groups in determining policies that affect working people on the job and in the diverse communities where they live.
Apply various theories and methods of how labor and community organizations influence the policy process to benefit their members and larger communities.
Assess state, federal, and international conditions as they influence public policy choices facing local governments.
Analyze written public policy on subjects of importance to diverse labor and community organizations.
Create a portfolio of public policy advocacy documents.

rows.title: Latin American Workers in the Americas
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize key commonalities and differences between the U.S. and Latin America in the development of the State and the political economy.
Assess the role of U.S. foreign policy in Latin America and its impact on Latin American workers' lives in the U.S. and Latin America.
Compare the development of labor movements in the U.S. and Latin America.
Analyze the processes of immigration from Latin America to the U.S. and its impact on the labor market.
Examine the problems facing the U.S. labor movement in its ability to address contemporary issues facing Latin American workers in both Latin America and the U.S.
Analyze the impact of class, race, and gender on the lives of Latin American workers in the Americas.

rows.title: Who Built America? From Reconstruction to the Present
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define the main developments in U.S. labor and working class history from the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era to the present.
Evaluate how the interactions between the working class, including organized labor, and other main social classes in the U.S. shaped the country from 1870 to today.
Identify the ways in which unions and workers' racial, ethnic, migration, and immigration status have influenced U.S. society and culture.
Analyze the organizations developed by working people to advance their interests, including the workers' civil rights or labor union movement.
Evaluate the relevance of U.S. labor and working class history to key social trends today.

rows.title: California Labor History
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the general outline of California labor history, including significant trends and social conflicts.
Evaluate and differentiate the experiences of different groups of working Californians.
Examine key organizations formed by California working people, including their key leaders, in their interactions with other social movements.
Assess California unionism's positive and negative aspects and effectiveness in helping working people.

rows.title: LGBT Culture & Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare LGBTQ+ social justice movements within the context of other social justice movements.
Analyze intersecting identities and problems with identity politics.
Interpret LGBTQ+ culture and society within decolonial contexts.
Analyze social investment in maintaining binaries.

rows.title: Contemporary LGBTQIA2+ Film
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the evolution of LGBTQIA2+ film from 1990 to the present in international and domestic films.
Analyze LGBTQIA2+ film as a medium of mass communication that reflects and influences beliefs about LGBTQIA2+ people and their communities.
Evaluate intersectional and theoretical approaches in the analysis of contemporary LGBTQIA2+ films.
Assess the cultural, ethical, political, and social contexts within which domestic and international LGBTQIA2+ films are created.

rows.title: Transgender Lives, Culture and Art
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the cultural, political, and social contexts within which transgender, non-binary, and gender diverse individuals have lived and created art and literature.
Evaluate the ways that societies and cultures around the world continue to inform transgender, non-binary, and gender-diverse identity, laws, and cultural acceptance.
Analyze art, artifacts, archival materials, and literature produced by transgender, non-binary, and gender-diverse people from different historical periods and geographic locations.
Analyze transphobic and rigid binary gendered structures related to imperialism and colonialism in different historical periods as reflected in art, law, literature, and medicine.

rows.title: Intimacy and Relationships between Women and Nonbinary People
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the impact of misogyny, the patriarchy, the gender binary, toxic masculinity, homophobia, and transphobia on lesbian, bisexual, pansexual, asexual, and queer relationships.
Analyze sexual power differences related to lesbian, bisexual, pansexual, asexual, and queer dating, intimacy, and sex.
Analyze the impact of systems of oppression on lesbian, bisexual, pansexual, asexual, and queer relationships.
Communicate clearly, listen effectively, and resolve conflicts with women and nonbinary people in dating and intimate relationships.
Compare ethics employed in social scientific inquiry regarding sexual identity formation, partner attraction, and communication patterns.

rows.title: Introduction to Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and write critically about the various ways people identify their sexual orientation and/or their gender identity and expression.
Analyze the systemic complexities confronting multiple intersecting identities within the context of LGBT struggles globally and domestically.
Assess theories about sexual orientation and gender identity and expression within the context of Feminist Theory, Gender Theory, and Queer Theory.
Examine the continuous evolution of legal policies and societal views of LGBT people on a global level.
Examine sexual orientation and gender identity issues within various indigenous, racial, ethnic, and recent immigrant communities in the United States.

rows.title: Contemporary Global Art and Culture
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze contemporary art and culture from different geographic locations to examine cultural, political, and social contexts within which LGBTQ+ individuals live and create various forms of art.
Examine contemporary homophobic and transphobic structures related to imperialism and colonialism in different global regions as reflected in art and culture.
Analyze various contemporary geographical centers of written and artistic expression and assess conditions in these centers that are conducive to freedom and creativity for LGBTQ+ artists.
Evaluate intersecting cultural identities and their importance to LGBTQ+ artistic expression and identity.

rows.title: LGBTQ+ Film: in the 1970s and 1980s
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the evolution of LGBTQ+ film in the 1970s and 1980s in international and domestic films.
Analyze film in the 1970s and 1980s as a medium of mass communication and its influence on values toward LGBTQ+ people and LGBTQ+ communities.
Evaluate intersectional and theoretical approaches in the analysis of LGBTQ+ films.
Assess the cultural, political, and social contexts in the creation of domestic and international films with LGBTQ+ themes.

rows.title: Introduction to Libraries and Library Resources
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret and apply classification systems.
Locate, use, and cite appropriate information resources for research.
Evaluate information resources based on standard qualitative criteria.
Describe basic library resources and systems.
Compare career paths in library services.

rows.title: Cataloging and Classification
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create descriptive catalog records, providing name and title access for library materials and using a variety of cataloging techniques.
Construct Dewey Decimal classification numbers, Library of Congress classification call numbers, and Library of Congress subject headings for library materials.
Code the catalog record into the appropriate format to be used by emerging library systems.
Debate the importance of cataloging to user access issues.
Distinguish career paths in library technical services.

rows.title: Computers in Libraries
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe basic deployment of computers, networks, and other digital technologies used in library services
Evaluate pros and cons of competing analog and digital services used in libraries
Analyze ethical and legal tensions impacting services, especially those in public institutions
Analyze evolving issues of access for diverse populations
Identify appropriate resources to obtain technical skills relevant to library work

rows.title: Special Libraries and Information Centers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discover and evaluate information resources and technologies specific to user needs in special libraries.
Distinguish between various types of special libraries, their functions, collections, and unique clientele.
Apply knowledge of subject headings or specific terminology for effective catalog, database, and web resource searching of special library topics.
Formulate reference responses specific to user needs in special libraries.
Compare roles and career opportunities for support staff working in special libraries.

rows.title: Library Work Experience
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe expectations for quality performance in the typical library workplace
Describe workplace health and safety precautions
Formulate personal work-based learning objectives
Develop a plan for continued professional development
Assess the steps for future career growth in library services

rows.title: PowerPoint Presentations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Plan and design a presentation that will effectively communicate a message to a target audience.
Select appropriate graphics and apply artistic effects.
Integrate appropriate tables, charts, and diagrams to enhance the presentation.
Produce a presentation using varied playback features and delivery formats.

rows.title: Storefront Apps for E-Business
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare industry standard e-store and mobile e-business apps.
Analyze the e-business operations and functions of an e-store app.
Appraise potential sales of a product or service.
Apply the skills needed to manage a prototype e-store or e-business.
Formulate search engine optimization (SEO) and a promotional strategy for an e-store or e-business.

rows.title: Mobile Apps for Business
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the most applicable mobile apps for a given business function.
Demonstrate how a selected mobile app can be applied in a given business context.
Organize a mobile strategy to improve productivity for a given business using apps.
Apply best practices for mobile marketing and brand promotion.

rows.title: Microsoft Outlook and OneNote
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use Microsoft Outlook and OneNote tools to increase workplace productivity and efficiency.
Integrate Outlook with other Microsoft Office programs to manage Contacts and create merged documents.
Organize and share projects, notes, meeting minutes, photos, and ideas using Microsoft OneNote.

rows.title: Database for Business/Microsoft Access
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Develop an Access database structure.
Manage tables using table relationships, primary keys, fields, and records.
Create queries using filters, selection criteria, calculated fields, and functions.
Create a custom form using form controls and tools.
Create a custom report using reoprt controls and tools.

rows.title: Short Calculus I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe, graph, and analyze polynomial, rational, and exponential functions and their inverses.
Interpret the concepts of limit, continuity, derivative, and integral in multiple ways.
Calculate derivatives of functions and apply differentiation to problems involving rates, linear approximation, graphing, and optimization.
Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals and apply integration to problems involving area and total change.

rows.title: Beginning Calculus
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define and interpret key calculus concepts, including limit, continuity, and derivative in multiple ways.
Evaluate limits and calculate derivatives.
Manipulate and graph functions, their transformations, and their respective inverse functions, and find the composite of two or more functions.

rows.title: Calculus I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply techniques of analytic geometry and calculus to analyze different types of functions and their inverses.
Define and interpret key calculus concepts, including limit, continuity, derivative, and definite integral of a function, in multiple ways.
Evaluate limits and calculate derivatives as well as appropriate antiderivatives and definite integrals.
Apply differentiation to solve a variety of problems by using techniques including linear approximation, related rates, graphing, and optimization.
Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to analyze the relationship between differentiation and integration.

rows.title: Calculus III
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze curves and surfaces in 3-dimensional space, especially by using vector methods.
Calculate and interpret partial derivatives and gradients and use these in applications, including rate of change, tangent planes, linear approximation, and optimization.
Set-up and evaluate multiple integrals in rectangular, polar, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates to find volumes and center of mass.
Set-up and evaluate line and surface integrals to find work and flux, respectively.
Interpret the physical meaning of the theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss and use these theorems to calculate various types of integrals.

rows.title: Linear Algebra
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define and apply real vector spaces and linear transformations.
Solve problems involving systems of linear equations and matrices.
Solve problems by working with the geometric structure of inner product spaces.
Prove basic linear algebra theorems.

rows.title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Solve problems involving vector spaces and linear transformations.
Prove linear algebra theorems.
Analyze, solve, and apply first and second-order linear differential equations.
Apply concepts of linear algebra to solve differential equations.

rows.title: Liberal Arts Math
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Exhibit mathematical fluency rooted in logic, set theory, and number theory.
Analyze and construct mathematical arguments and proofs.
Apply mathematical principles to solve problems involving finance and probability.

rows.title: Precalculus Algebra
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define, graph, interpret, and apply functions, their transformations, and their respective inverse functions.
Construct functions to model and analyze real-world situations.
Describe and graph polynomial, rational, exponential and logarithmic functions and apply their properties to solve equations and applications.
Identify, compare, and contrast the equations, graphs, and properties of conic sections.

rows.title: Precalculus & Trigonometry
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct functions to model and analyze real-world situations.
Manipulate and apply functions, their transformations, and their respective inverse functions.
Describe and graph various types of functions and apply their properties to solve linear and nonlinear equations and inequalities.
Recognize the equations, graphs, and properties of conic sections.
Simplify and evaluate expressions by applying trigonometric identities.

rows.title: The Electronic Health Record
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the major components of government health and electronic record initiatives, administrative workflows, and an electronic health record (EHR).
Compare coding classification systems and distinguish their relationship to the patient visit.
Describe the core functions of an electronic health record and the electronic health record framework.
Explain the patient visit functions and workflow for a medical encounter.
Manage patient encounters by completing the demographic, medical, and scheduling documentation and updating the EHR.

rows.title: Communication and Professionalism in Health Care
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze interpersonal skills in relation to personal and professional interactions
Evaluate types of professional communication within a healthcare organization
Employ a variety of communication techniques in response to patients' healthcare needs
Apply legal, licensure, and safety regulations to the provision of clinical patient care

rows.title: Electronic Management of Financial Medical Records
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define bookkeeping and computer vocabulary associated with medical billing.
Create and edit patient accounts, insurance claim forms, financial reports and business correspondence.
Abstract medical records for data required to complete insurance claims
Describe banking, accounts payable, and collections procedures performed in a medical office.
Demonstrate professionalism and sensitivity when interacting with providers, patients, and third party representatives regarding financial obligations.

rows.title: Advanced Medical Billing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the differences between Health Care Facilities and Ambulatory Surgery Centers billing and coding practices and the professional, inpatient and outpatient services.
Explain the revenue cycle of reimbursement systems for ambulatory surgery centers and hospital facility claims.
Research insurance company policies as they pertain to patient's health benefits and billing requirements.
Describe the tools used to comply with Medicare and Medicaid regulations for billing and coding for inpatient and outpatient services.
Explain and compare the various coding certification examinations and credentials.

rows.title: Organizational Behavior for Supervisors
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare approaches to organizational behavior in the workplace.
Apply the manager's functions, leadership style, roles and skills to diverse situations.
Distinguish among appropriate motivational theories for management.
Manage organizational change using leadership and control functions.

rows.title: Business Communication
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compose emails, reports, proposals, and other business documents with proper grammar, tone, and formatting.
Organize and present clear, concise, and engaging business presentations using verbal and nonverbal communication strategies while integrating visual aids and technology.
Apply effective communication strategies to foster collaboration, resolve conflicts, and adapt messaging for diverse audiences in global and multicultural business environments.
Assess and implement appropriate digital and social media communication strategies for professional networking, corporate messaging, and customer engagement.

rows.title: Bicycle Maintenance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply basic tools, techniques and trouble-shooting strategies for making bicycle repairs.
Execute a wide variety of repairs or adjustment to a variety of bicycles.
Perform a bicycle safety inspection and demonstrate road and shop safety.
Identify types of bicycles and fit them to riders.

rows.title: Motorcycle General Service
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply fundamental carburetor and electronic fuel injection principles to service and repair procedures.
Describe service principles of two-stroke and four-stroke engine lubrication systems and analyze effects on performance and engine longevity of different oil types.
Troubleshoot chassis, suspension, tires and brake systems to diagnose complaints and repair to conform with industry-standard service requirements.

rows.title: Engine & Power Train Repair
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Utilize service manuals correctly and special tools safely in the process of achieving a professional standard rebuild.
Compare the construction and performance of four stroke and two stroke engines.
Troubleshoot engine repair needs by disassembling an engine, measuring critical components, and interpreting evidence of failure.
Rebuild engines and power trains to factory-approved standards, perform operational checks, and make final adjustments after assembly.

rows.title: Introduction to Marketing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the key marketing management philosophies as they relate to marketing within an ethical society.
Compare methods used for accessing the external marketing environment as it relates to the consumer decision-making process.
Analyze the strategic planning process necessary to create a competitive advantage to a given target market.
Integrate the elements of the marketing mix to create a sustainable, competitive advantage.
Integrate the elements of social media marketing strategies into a brand's overall marketing mix.
Produce a written marketing plan that demonstrates an understanding of core marketing strategies.

rows.title: Advertising and Integrated Marketing Communication
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the principles and value of an integrated marketing communication and advertising program and its role in the overall marketing plan.
Apply the factors of building a desired corporate image or powerful brand.
Deliver an effective written advertising and integrated marketing communications plan.

rows.title: Music Fundamentals
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Translate beginning level music notation examples into sound through rhythmic or singing performance.
Write beginning-level music notation transcriptions of specific rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic patterns at a beginning level.
Discriminate between simple and compound meter in notation and sound examples at a beginning level.
Evaluate harmonic functions and construct properly noted scales, intervals, triads and seventh chords at a beginning level.
Articulate various melodic modes and scales from diverse historical and cultural contexts at a beginning level.

rows.title: Guitar Workshop
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform skills appropriate for intermediate to advanced guitar ensembles.
Prepare and perform a variety of musical roles within the guitar ensemble.
Prepare and perform right-hand techniques suitable for intermediate to advanced repertoire in various styles.
Synthesize knowledge of chordal structure and theory in the performance of intermediate to advanced level guitar ensemble music.
Analyze and explain the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic elements that comprise guitar ensemble repertoire.

rows.title: Jazz/Rock Improvisation Workshop
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Prepare and perform music in a variety of jazz, rock and blues settings as a soloist and as part of an ensemble
Demonstrate basic techniques of improvisation in the jazz, rock and/or related genres
Compare nuances of style between leading figures in the jazz, rock and/or related genres
Interpret well-known musical selections in the jazz, rock and/or related genres in a developing personal style

rows.title: Orchestra
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Prepare and perform orchestral or world music repertoire.
Identify and play the correct pitches with accurate intonation in an orchestral context.
Apply appropriate preparation and performance skills to performances of orchestral or world music repertoire.
Synthesize knowledge of musical structures and theories in the performance of orchestral repertoire.
Analyze and explain the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic elements that comprise orchestral repertoire.

rows.title: Brass Ensemble
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform skills appropriate for intermediate to advanced brass ensembles.
Prepare and perform a variety of musical roles within the brass ensemble.
Interpret a variety of style characteristics appropriate to the brass ensemble repertoire in a performance.
Analyze and explain the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic elements that comprise brass ensemble repertoire.

rows.title: Intermediate Musicianship
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Sing a chromatic or modulating melody at first sight
Notate a chromatic or modulating melody in dictation
Perform rhythmic drills in two parts using both hands
Notate syncopated and irregularly subdivided rhythm in dictation
Notate the outer parts and identify the harmonies in four-part dictation
Sing a chromatic or modulating melody while playing an independent accompaniment on the piano using both hands

rows.title: Traditional African Music
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the development of traditional African music as a mode of expression useful in many types of communication
Articulate the role of music structures in African societies as part of an overall African philosophy
Appraise the cultural and social values of African music
Differentiate between religious and secular African music

rows.title: History of Music in Western Culture: Romanticism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the historical roots of Western musical culture during the Romantic Period
Compare music prior to the 19th century to music within the Romantic Era with respect to tonal structure, historical development, and aesthetic value
Identify religions, philosophies, and lifestyles of the Romantic Era
Assess the major stylistic developments of music within the Romantic Period
Identify Romantic Era musical instruments as represented in photographs, drawings, and recordings

rows.title: Music of East Asia
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare East Asian and Western music with respect to tonal structure, historical development, and aesthetic value.
Identify religions, philosophies and a brief historical overview of the three East Asian countries through the ages.
Assess the minor stylistic theatrical developments of East Asian Music.
Identify East Asian musical instruments.
Analyze the historical roots of China, Korea, and Japan, focusing on the musical aspects.

rows.title: Music in American Culture
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare musical cultures in America, including their origins, styles and interaction.
Analyze historical roots of American musical cultures.
Analyze the influence of religion, society or culture on American musical cultures.
Assess the major developments in and characteristics of American musical styles studied
Identify and describe musical instruments used in music of America.

rows.title: Survey of Opera and Musical Theater
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify operas and musical theater from different historical eras and the musical styles of their representative composers
Describe the development of opera and musical theater within social, cultural, and political contexts
Apply correct terminology in discussing opera and musical theater
Evaluate opera and musical theater performances and overall effectiveness of production

rows.title: Chromatic Harmony
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the large scale structures as well as harmonies in printed excerpts of primarily 19th-century Western European music using Roman numerals and figures and considering cultural contexts

Compose either the upper or lower three parts of a four-part chorale based on a given chromatic and/or modulating bass or melody, choosing stylistically appropriate chromatically-altered chords and/or modulation techniques
Compose the upper three parts of a modulating chorale from figured bass symbols, choosing stylistically appropriate chromatically-altered chords and/or modulation techniques
Arrange a modulating four-part harmonization into an instrumental or vocal composition in ternary form

rows.title: Beginning Classical Guitar
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and apply classical guitar technique and musicianship at a beginning level
Diagram and perform commonly used beginning level chords
Summarize the basic construction, adjustment and care of the guitar
Assess critical aspects of basic right-hand arpeggio and strum techniques
Select beginning repertoire for practice and performance

rows.title: Beginning Violin
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and apply violin technique and musicianship at a beginning level.
Diagram and perform selected scale and interval exercises in beginning level positions.
Interpret and perform beginning melodies, melodic passages or melodic fragments according to accepted standards.
Select appropriate beginning repertoire for practice and performance.
Explain the general construction, adjustment and care of the violin.
Demonstrate critical aspects of bow grip and left-hand technique according to accepted standards.

rows.title: Beginning Jazz & Other Popular Piano
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Prepare and play a piece of music from the standard jazz piano repertoire.
Formulate basic popular piano harmony for a given melody.
Prepare a melody in various ways using rhythmical variation.
Assemble elementary left hand piano accompaniments integrating right hand melodic material.
Differentiate and construct stylistic differences in playing jazz, blues, Brazilian, Afro-Cuban and other musical styles.

rows.title: Intermediate Piano
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the structure and study the composer of a chosen piece.
Prepare and perform piano music at an intermediate level.
Employ touch control, proper phrasing and pedaling in a stylistically appropriate manner suitable to the genre, period and style of the literature.
Prepare and perform a selection of music from the standard intermediate level piano repertoire.
Sight read intermediate-level piano music charts.

rows.title: Introduction to Native American Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze critically the intersection of race and racism as they relate to class, gender, sexuality, religion, spirituality, sovereignty, ability, tribal citizenship, language, and/or age in Native American and Indigenous communities.
Examine the diversity of Native American and Indigenous peoples, including knowledge systems, spirituality, governance structures, land stewardship, and cultural production.
Assess the political, economic, and cultural dispossession on Native American and Indigenous communities perpetrated by European invasion and settler-colonialism.

Evaluate how resistance, activism, racial and social justice, solidarity, and liberation, as experienced and enacted by Native Americans, are relevant to current and structural issues, including self-determination and sovereignty, repatriation, and cultural revival.

rows.title: Pharmacology in Nursing Part I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply general principles of pharmacology in a clinical setting.
Utilize up to date practice models linking knowledge of dosage and potential adverse outcomes in pharmacologic care.
Demonstrate nursing process literacy by linking patient data with drug information to develop a nursing diagnosis.
Plan the safe management of drug administration
Evaluate a nursing plan of care reflecting patient centered goals associated with drug therapy
Design individualized nursing care plans including concepts of cultural and genetic variability awareness in pharmacologic care.

rows.title: Nursing Skills Lab
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify fundamental nursing skills and organize supplies/equipment to meet the specific situations and conditions of the acute and chronically ill adult.
Apply the role and responsibilities of the nurse as a member of the health care team through appropriate knowledge, skills and attitudes.
Describe the theoretical basis of and perform selected fundamental nursing skills competently, using attitudes of care, respect, dignity, and professionalism.
Collect accurate data to conduct a priority-based physical assessment on an adult with consideration of the age continuum.
Synthesize knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to provide effective communication for direct patient care in a safe and effective manner.

rows.title: Intermediate Nursing Skills
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Prepare for the professional clinical role by adhering to evidence-based standards of practice, legal constraints, and ethical practices with respect to National Patient Safety goals.
Identify abnormal assessment findings and data to develop priority-based patient-centered interventions to improve patient care outcomes.
Apply evidence-based clinical judgment and decision-making to safely perform intermediate nursing skills and procedures for adult and older adult patients.

Communicate clearly and effectively with members of the health care team in simulation activities with focus on open communication, mutual respect, collaboration, and shared decision-making to achieve safety and quality patient care.

rows.title: Nursing of Children
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Synthesize information from principles and major theories of development and family-centered care into the nursing process to support optimum child health and development.
Describe the pathophysiology, etiology, clinical manifestations, and nursing management for the common diseases and injuries affecting children and the adolescent population.
Identify legal and ethical aspects of providing nursing care.
Employ nursing skills to provide direct patient care in a safe and effective manner.
Apply the nursing process and evidence-based clinical reasoning in diverse pediatric nursing settings.

rows.title: Advanced Medical-Surgical Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the principles of leadership and management theories and demonstrate self-reliance and progressive independence in managing a group of patients utilizing evidence-based practices.
Identify and provide safe, culturally sensitive, and family-centered care across the lifespan in various healthcare settings.
Work effectively with diverse healthcare teams to improve patient outcomes.
Use information and technology for effective communication and decision making.
Apply ethical, equitable principles, and legal considerations in nursing practice.

rows.title: Oceanography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply scientific inquiry and investigation of evidence to critically evaluate oceanographic principles.
Communicate oceanographic ideas and theories effectively.
Apply scientific principles, theories, or models to explain the behavior of oceanographic phenomena.
Evaluate human interactions with the oceans and the societal impacts.

rows.title: Sports in Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain historical contexts and social theories as they relate to sports.
Analyze factors and issues that affect the interaction of sports and society.
Summarize how sports shape and are shaped by ideologies and values.
