rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the fundamental laws of electromagnetism to investigate and assess physical phenomena that impact society.
Use mathematics up to and including calculus to solve electromagnetism problems.
Communicate physics concepts, processes, and results effectively.

rows.title: Waves and Thermodynamics for Scientists and Engineers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the fundamental laws of waves and thermodynamics to investigate and assess physical phenomena that impact society.
Use mathematics up to and including calculus to solve waves and thermodynamics problems.
Communicate physics concepts, processes, and results effectively.

rows.title: Modern Physics for Scientists and Engineers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate concepts, processes, and results from physics effectively.
Apply the fundamental laws of modem physics to investigate and assess physical phenomena that impact society.
Use mathematics up to and including calculus to solve modem physics problems.

rows.title: Elementary Filipino (Tagalog)
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret spoken and written Filipino (Tagalog) at the elementary level.
Write short communications incorporating the main markers and verb inflections of the Filipino (Tagalog) language.
Communicate orally in basic everyday situations using a range of Filipino (Tagalog) grammatical structures with accurate pronunciation and intonation.
Explain elements of Philippine culture at an appropriate level for a basic beginning Filipino (Tagalog) language learner.
Use Filipino expressions to indicate respect or formality in various situations.

rows.title: Ethnic Politics in the United States
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the relationship between racial/ethnic identity and politics.

Compare the political experience, organization, and participatory behavior at least three of African-Americans, Latino/Hispanic Americans, Asian-Americans, Indigenous/First Nations Americans and European-Americans.
Utilize diverse political theoretical approaches to understand ethnic politics, including liberalism/pluralism, conservatism, socialism, and post-modern theories.
Discuss the salient policy issues that affect and direct ethnic political activity.
Analyze multiracial politics and identity.

rows.title: Government & Politics of Latin America
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the political systems, ideologies, and governments in Latin America.
Examine the political economy of Latin America and its impact on society, including external influences, and U.S. interactions.
Critique the role of Latin America's international relations with the US and other countries.
Assess the role of important political forces in Latin America.
Analyze comparative political systems and government institutions as well as cultural components in shaping these systems.

rows.title: Comparative Government
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate texts and ideas in the field of Comparative Politics.
Apply the comparative method to identifying and explaining similarities and differences among various political thoughts and actions throughout the world.
Compare a variety of political and political economic systems, both in theory and with country examples.
Distinguish among regime types and their central features, with a focus on democratic regimes
Explain the impact of the regional, environmental, economic, historical and cultural factors on political behavior and institutions.

rows.title: Political Theory
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the study of political theory to political life, political institutions, and important political phenomena, including issues of identity.
Analyze political theory through diverse foundational texts reflecting political values and beliefs across time and cultures.
Assess the origins of political theories, ancient, modern, and contemporary in the historical and social contexts surrounding them.
Explain the defining elements and assumptions of major political theories and ideologies, especially liberalism and conservatism.

rows.title: Independent Studies in Political Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and discuss topics under consideration in the individual political science study.
Utilize social sciences research methods and primary and secondary sources to develop an argument or interpretation.

rows.title: Middle East Governments and Politics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the structure and functioning of the governments and political systems in the Middle East and North Africa.
Assess current political issues, events, and actors in the Middle East.
Identify and compare the human rights conditions of ethnic, racial, and religious minority groups, women, and LGBT persons across the countries of the Middle East.
Analyze Middle East governments and politics by selecting and using appropriate comparative Political Science methodologies and approaches, including the use of primary sources.

rows.title: American Government and Politics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the founding and development of the U.S. and California Constitution.
Critique governing institutions and political processes within the United States and California.
Employ introductory political science research methods to contextualize contemporary political issues and operations in the United States and California.
Assess civil liberties and civil rights of individuals and groups as articulated in the U.S. and California Constitutions and subsequent court decisions.
Investigate the role of identity and political ideology in shaping public opinion and public policy in the United States and California.
Analyze how to effectively participate in politics at the national, state, county, and/or city levels.

rows.title: Theories of Personality
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and apply basic terms and definitions in personality psychology
Evaluate the methods of studying personality
Describe and evaluate the intersectionality of culture, race, and/or gender in personality theory
Compare major personality theories
Apply the major personality theories to explain the personalities of self and/or others

rows.title: Assertive Behavior
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate between assertive, aggressive, passive, and passive-aggressive behavior.
Identify psychological and emotional barriers to assertive behavior.
Describe the psychological effects of socialization, gender, and culture on assertiveness and how assertiveness is viewed.
Apply cognitive-behavioral psychology techniques and strategies for overcoming barriers to assertive behavior.

rows.title: Biological Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the central features of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, and the endocrine system and their relationship to psychological phenomena.
Apply basic terms and concepts used in biological psychology.
Apply different levels of analysis including biological, cognitive, sociocultural, and theoretical to explain normal and abnormal psychological behaviors and mental processes.
Evaluate current research design and findings in biological psychology.

rows.title: Lifespan Development
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare major theoretical perspectives used to explain human development from conception through death.
Explain the primary developmental tasks associated with different periods of the lifespan.
Analyze the interaction of different areas of development and how such interaction affects developmental outcomes.
Evaluate the effects of the multiple and diverse contexts in which development occurs.
Apply developmental concepts, theories, and research findings to the developing person.

rows.title: Queer Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain distinctions among various sexual and gender minorities.
Apply current theories and empirical research to sexual orientation and gender diversity.
Analyze the social construction of sexual orientation and gender.
Evaluate the causes of stigma and their impact on sexual and gender minorities.

rows.title: Applied Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe key psychological concepts, theories, and research findings relevant to human adjustment.
Apply psychological principles that can facilitate and support personal human adjustment in various life contexts and experiences.
Analyze strategies and interventions that can facilitate psychological adjustment and address common adjustment challenges.
Evaluate the impact of sociocultural forces on individual psychological adjustment and overall emotional well-being.

rows.title: Forensic Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe how psychologists influence the legal process through research, expert testimony, and as consultants and practitioners.
Compare the methods and goals of psychology and the legal system.
Evaluate psychological research, theory, practice, and methodology as applied to a legal issue.
Analyze landmark court decisions and the underlying assumptions about behavior.
Analyze the opposing arguments of psycholegal issues in an objective way.

rows.title: Statistics for Behavioral Sciences
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply statistical concepts and describe how they affect the interpretation of specific analyses, including interpreting the statistical significance of p values.
Utilize calculators and/or computer software to perform various statistical tests.
Analyze the strengths and weaknesses of research findings given how data is collected and analyzed in the behavioral sciences.
Assess statistical analysis for appropriateness given the level or scale of measurement of a variable.
Distinguish between experimental and correlational methods in terms of their respective assumptions, interpretations, and limitations in the behavioral sciences.

Use appropriate statistical techniques to analyze and interpret applications based on data from behavioral sciences, economics, social science, psychology, political science, administration of justice, life science, physical science, health science, education and other related fields.

rows.title: Psychology of Stress
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate between types of acute and chronic stress.
Interpret stress physiology and how stress impacts physical and mental health.
Analyze circumstances that influence stress reactivity and life satisfaction.
Describe and apply both active and palliative coping strategies for stress.

rows.title: Fire Safety Director
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define the role and responsibilities of the Fire Safety Director position
Define what qualifies as a high rise building and what occupancies require a Fire Safety Director as required by law
Perform required evolutions for emergency evacuation for relocation in a high-rise building

Train members of the emergency response team and floor warden organization in the identification and use of facility fire safety equipment; evacuation needs of the physically disabled; emergency communications, and appropriate actions to be taken during emergencies

rows.title: Fire Training Work Experience II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply Firefighter I knowledge and skills to emergency and non-emergency situations.
Analyze dangerous situations and assist with retrieving appropriate tools and equipment for fire personnel.
Use tools and equipment according to the National Fire Protection Association's Standard 1001 for Firefighter I.
Explain the importance of teamwork at emergency incidents and non-emergency training.
Assess patients and use appropriate medical protocols in a firefighter response situation.

rows.title: Conceptual Physical Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate physical science arguments in a critical manner through the application of scientific inquiry and investigation of evidence.
Communicate scientific ideas and theories effectively.
Explain the behavior of natural physical phenomena through the application of scientific principles, theories, or models.
Apply physical science knowledge and reasoning to human interaction with the natural world and issues impacting society.

rows.title: Firefighter One Academy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for firefighting and rescue
Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for wildland fire fighting
Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter One curriculum for hazardous materials
Execute job knowledge and performance specific to the State Fire Training Firefighter Two curriculum for firefighting and rescue

rows.title: Incident Command System ICS 400: Advanced ICS Command and General Staff-Complex Incidents
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain how major incidents pose special management challenges and demonstrate how to organize and manage those incidents.
Describe the circumstances in which an area command is established and show how to organize and manage these incidents.
Describe with examples the circumstances in which multi-agency coordination systems are established.

rows.title: Fire Service Career Preparation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify fields of interest or career paths within fire service organizations and develop a plan for self-study and group study.
Describe educational and vocational training resources related to the fire service as part of a career educational plan to prepare for the fire service application process.
Locate entry-level fire service job announcements and employment opportunities.
Articulate the three major components of the fire service entrance exams and key areas of study for each component.

rows.title: Introduction to Fire Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and explain the use of fire service equipment and apparatuses and how they are used in fire suppression operations.
Describe fire service organizational structures, Incident Command Systems (ICS), and communication systems that support the fire service organization.
Evaluate operational and training safety practices that focus on firefighter health and safety.
Explain fire dynamics and their effects in fire incidents as related to firefighting operations.
Compare fire prevention, fire investigation, medical services and other specialty fire service programs designed to protect the public.

rows.title: Fire Protection Equipment & Systems
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the chemistry and physics of fire behavior relevant to fire protection equipment and systems.
Describe the principles and characteristics of fire detection and alarm systems and fire equipment and suppression systems.
Explain the effects of smoke control management systems in buildings.
Explain the various fire protection and detection systems within a building that contribute to fire and life safety.

rows.title: Wildland Fire Control
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify fuels, topography, weather, and fire behavior as they relate to wildland fire incidents
Explain the various approaches to control and extinguish wildland fires
Describe specific safety considerations connected with wildland firefighting such as personnel safety, fire behavior, and proper use of equipment and tools
Compare the factors affecting wildland fires with the recognized tactics employed to extinguish wildland fires

rows.title: Introduction to Fire Prevention
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze fire prevention efforts as they relate to fire loss data.
Examine the need, responsibilities, and importance of fire prevention for public and private fire prevention organizations.
Classify minimum professional qualifications and training at the state and national level for fire inspectors, fire investigators, and public educators.
Differentiate the elements of a new project construction plan review program.
Distinguish laws, rules, codes, and other regulations relevant to fire protection and the authority having jurisdiction.

rows.title: Vehicle Extrication
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess a vehicle accident scene utilizing safety considerations and the use of the Incident Command System (ICS)
Evaluate vehicle stabilization techniques, vehicle access and egress, rescue access and egress options for a vehicle accident
Remove victims to a safe area using vehicle extrication tools and equipment

rows.title: Hazardous Materials First Responder Operations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the chemical and physical properties of hazardous materials and the health hazards associated with chemical releases.
Interpret the key components and use of the Emergency Response Guidebook.
Evaluate protective equipment and measures to be taken during a hazardous materials incident.

rows.title: Company Officer 2B: General Administrative Functions
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Articulate state and federal laws and regulations pertaining to fire service supervisors and the risks of civil and criminal liability for violations of these rules.
Formulate the purpose of each management component of the organization.
Devise a budget and purchasing process that complies with local governmental guidelines.
Describe the need for collecting incident-response data that is accurate and timely to determine incident trending.

rows.title: Company Officer 2D: All-Risk Command Operations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Develop and implement an incident action plan involving single and multi-unit operations that might include a fire incident or non-fire incident.

Complete incident command form 201 that employs principles of command, resource management, emergency operations, scene conditions, local emergency plans, local evacuation, allocation of resources, and evaluation of fire behavior.
Implement a plan of action for emergencies based on the National Fire Protections Standard 1600 for disasters, emergency, and business continuity plans.
Manage a post-analysis of an emergency incident that lists the elements, describes the events that occurred, and suggests actions in similar future incidents.

rows.title: Instructor I - State Fire Trng
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ the Four-Step Method of Vocational Instruction to provide instruction in fire training principles.
Analyze an existing lesson plan and adapt it to present an effective psychomotor or technical lesson.
Organize the educational environment so that it is conducive to learning.
Produce peer feedback to student instructors that encourages positive instructional techniques and identifies aspects that need improvement.
Administer oral, written, and performance exams in a manner that eliminates bias and discrimination, follows correct procedures, and maintains security of test materials.

rows.title: Intro to Social Work and Human Services
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss the historical evolution and current state of social welfare and human services in the United States.
Explain the current service delivery system environment that addresses social work and human service clients’ needs.
Analyze contemporary social issues that impact social welfare and human service agencies and institutions.
Describe the ethical responsibilities of working with social work and human service organizations with attention to cultural humility and oppressed groups.
Explain the research methods used to inform and evaluate social work practice.

rows.title: Social Work Practicum
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the major components of social work and human services to a practice setting.

Apply knowledge of the National Association of Social Work (NASW) Code of Ethics, fundamental legal guidelines, privacy, and information management related to professional practice within specific agency settings.
Demonstrate personal self-awareness, the practice of non-judgmental assessment, cultural engagement, and support capability.
Demonstrate professional development through the incorporation of feedback from supervision.

rows.title: Introduction to Research Methods
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the complexities of research ethics in scientific inquiry.
Apply quantitative and qualitative research methods to examine sociological questions.
Explain and use basic descriptive and inferential statistical analyses.
Compare how theories, concepts, and hypotheses are employed in qualitative and quantitative research designs.

rows.title: Social Problems
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Articulate major problems affecting society employing a sociological perspective.
Integrate sociological theories and concepts to explore the social construction of social problems.
Analyze quantitative and qualitative data to determine the consequences of social problems.
Analyze actions that address social problems using sociological approaches.

rows.title: Men, Masculinity, and Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply theories and research methods in the study of masculinities in culture and society.
Compare key intersectional frameworks that influence the perceptions and experiences of masculinity in social contexts.
Analyze the major social institutions and practices that construct masculine roles and how these constructions interact with one another.
Assess how the sociological perspective contributes to the understanding of accepted masculinity’s power to create difference and inequality

rows.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze how race and ethnicity, as social institutions and critical ethnic studies concepts, organize social life across multiple dimensions.
Illustrate the specific mechanisms by which categories and ideas of race and ethnicity are constructed through lived experiences, policies, cultural practices, and representations.

Apply theories and frameworks from the disciplines of Sociology and Ethnic Studies to the lived experiences and social struggles of African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and/or Latino/a Americans in order to analyze and reframe topical contemporary discussions about racial-ethnic identity and racism.

Evaluate social scientific data on African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and/or Latino/a Americans concerning various forms of racial and ethnic prejudice, discrimination, and privilege to develop sociological and ethnic studies explanations for their causes and impacts.

Articulate the ways that knowledge produced by African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and/or Latino/a American communities have engaged with race and ethnicity as symbols across multiple social institutions with the goals of establishing sovereignty, equality and racial justice.

rows.title: Beginning Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intelligible pronunciation and intonation at a novice level when talking about personal or university-life situations.
Use accurate grammatical structures in Spanish at a novice level to describe people, places, and things, or to express likes and dislikes.
Respond effectively to spoken Spanish with appropriate grammatical forms, accurate vocabulary, and clear pronunciation at a novice level.
Communicate in Spanish in an appropriate and effective manner on cultural topics related to the evolution of the language or family and community traditions in the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Intermediate Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Express ideas and opinions effectively in Spanish at an intermediate level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation.
Use accurate grammatical structures in Spanish at an intermediate level to express wishes, subjective reactions, uncertainty and personal opinions.
Interpret spoken Spanish at an intermediate level when presented with present, past or future events, in hypothetical or subjective situations.

Compare socioeconomic and cultural differences between Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures in the context of racial and social diversity, artistic expressions, migrations, and environmental impacts of climate change.

rows.title: Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish at a novice-mid level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation and intonation
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Spanish at a novice-mid level
Compose short written communications in Spanish incorporating the principles of present tense syntax at the novice-mid level
Articulate aspects of the cultures of the Spanish-speaking world areas and communities

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level with accurate grammatical structures, intelligible pronunciation, and clear intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of Spanish grammar and syntax at a mid-intermediate level.
Compare aspects of Latin America and Spanish Peninsular cultures and societies.

rows.title: Grammar Review and Composition
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use complex structures to interact orally in Spanish and synthesize information with near-native fluency.
Apply editing skills to revise Spanish errors in grammar, punctuation, and word usage.
Summarize and organize arguments effectively with near-native fluency.
Explain select cultural, social and political issues in the Spanish-speaking world.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Spanish at a low-intermediate level with accurate grammatical structures, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate low level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of Spanish grammar and syntax at an intermediate low level.
Compare aspects of Latin America and Spanish Peninsular cultures and societies.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at an intermediate-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate-high level
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present syntax in indicative and subjunctive modes at a intermediate-high level.
Articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures at an intermediate-high level.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 1A
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the grammar and syntax structures of language, assessing differences between formal and informal registers.
Produce written pieces utilizing accurate grammar, structure and enriched vocabulary, while avoiding literal translation and interference from English.
Communicate effectively using an enriched vocabulary as well as different registers of the language, and identify the significance these registers have in the professional world.
Analyze new perspectives of the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world under a wide historical, artistic, and social background.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 2
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and synthesize Spanish grammar structures and syntax rules using linguistic knowledge to infer spelling, time frames, and sentence construction.

Communicate in writing with enriched Spanish vocabulary and complex syntax producing full paragraphs that are organized and detailed, providing a well-supported argument, without interference with English.
Express thoughts efficiently on topics of personal and community interest using a broad range of vocabulary and high-frequency structures.
Compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries of the Andean and Southern Cone regions.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 2B
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and synthesize Spanish grammar structures and syntax rules using linguistic knowledge to infer spelling, time frames, and sentence construction.

Communicate in writing with enriched Spanish vocabulary and complex syntax producing full paragraphs that are organized and detailed, providing a well-supported argument, without interference with English.
Express thoughts efficiently on topics of personal and community interest using a broad range of vocabulary and high-frequency structures.
Compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries of the Andean and Southern Cone regions.

rows.title: Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Spanish at an intermediate-high level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate-high level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of past and present syntax in indicative and subjunctive modes at a intermediate-high level.
Articulate aspects of Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures at an intermediate-high level.

rows.title: Advanced Spanish: Hispanic Culture and Civilization
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish about Hispanic cultures.
Analyze critically significant issues of each chronological period of Hispanic civilization from the beginning of its history through the 17th century.
Identify historical figures and moments of the Hispanic cultures and civilization from the beginning of its history through the 17th century.
Compare Spanish, Hispanic American, and Hispanic cultures from the beginning of its history through the 17th century.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Converse on diverse topics expressing personal ideas demonstrating language fluency at the intermediate-advanced level.
Interpret written texts on a variety of personal, cultural or social topics at an intermediate-advanced level.
Compose written texts using complex grammar structures, accurate syntax and punctuation on a variety of personal, cultural or social topics at the intermediate-advanced level.
Analyze at an intermediate-advanced level historical and cultural elements and issues from the Spanish-speaking world to interpret and describe societal differences and diverse viewpoints.

rows.title: Intro to Literature in Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze a literary passage in terms of style and content and within a cultural context.
Integrate and apply new vocabulary and introductory concepts of literary criticism and literary history in the interpretation of Spanish literature.
Compare literary movements and authors within the larger context of Hispanic cultures and literature.
Identify and explain the distinctive components of literary genres produced in Spanish-speaking cultures and how each one conveys a message in a different manner.

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess how data were collected and recognize how data collection affects what conclusions can be drawn from the data.
Identify appropriate graphs and summary statistics for variables and relationships between them and correctly interpret information from graphs and summary statistics.
Describe and apply probability concepts and distributions.
Demonstrate an understanding of, and ability to use, basic ideas of statistical processes, including hypothesis tests and confidence interval estimation.
Identify appropriate statistical techniques and use technology-based statistical analysis to describe, interpret, and communicate results.
Evaluate ethical issues in statistical practice.

rows.title: Custodial Training for Healthcare Workers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and assess the health risks related to custodial work in the healthcare industry.
Apply industry-standard techniques and approved procedures while cleaning healthcare sites and disposing of waste.
Explain patients' rights and interface with them appropriately.

rows.title: Orientation to Visual Media Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Research and discuss career opportunities in visual communication fields
Identify a degree or certificate program in Visual Media Design that would support career goals
Assess resources for academic success and career search in visual communication fields

rows.title: Design Thinking
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use design thinking as a mindset and a process.
Identify the drivers and barriers to design thinking.
Apply strategies to develop design solutions.

rows.title: History of Graphic Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify significant movements in graphic design history.
Analyze and interpret images, symbols, and typography historically used in visual communication, using design language.
Evaluate the influence of technological, commercial and societal factors on graphic design work.

rows.title: Color in Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explore, describe and differentiate the color models, processes and materials used with the various fields of design.
Utilize colors and color harmonies in formal compositions produced with both analog and digital tools.
Analyze and compare the historical, cultural, psychological, symbolic and personal uses of color in their own design work and the work of others.
Employ an iterative design process in individual and collaborative design activities.

rows.title: Graphic Design II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Design and develop solutions for a range of interactive and complex print projects.
Analyze and critically discuss the strengths and weaknesses of interactive and static design solutions.
Present and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: Package Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss the function of package design in advertising communication.
Identify the target market and evaluate its role in relationship to design solutions.
Apply and demonstrate compositional skills working with type, color, pattern and 3-dimensional form in building comps and models.
Employ critical thinking and communication skills in the development of package design solutions, using relevant concepts and terminology.
Employ and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: User Experience
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ industry-standard tools used in User Experience design.
Employ UX design process models in developing design solutions.
Present and justify design decisions using relevant User Experience design concepts and vocabulary.
Critique user experience design verbally and in writing.

rows.title: Typography II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ aspects of fine typography for screen and print.
Select appropriate typefaces, font formats and digital tools for screen and print typography.
Discuss historical and contemporary classification, typefaces, designers, and foundries.
Use an iterative design process to solve communication problems, working both individually and collaboratively.
Critique the merits of various design solutions using design and type terminology and concepts.

rows.title: Web Production II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Design responsive web content using industry best practices
Critique and discuss responsive projects in terms of usability and accessibility
Employ an iterative design process to produce a responsive web project

rows.title: Illustrator II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct complex Illustrator files using industry-standard best practices and advanced features.
Integrate artwork from Adobe Illustrator into other image-creation software.
Employ an iterative process when producing original work.
Assess design solutions and articulate their strengths and weaknesses.

rows.title: Adobe InDesign: Publication Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct complex multi-page documents following industry best practices for layout and typesetting.
Use an iterative design process to create professional-level publications using Adobe InDesign.
Assess design solutions and articulate their strengths and weaknesses.

rows.title: Photoshop II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct complex Photoshop files using industry-standard best practices and advanced features.
Analyze and reproduce complex Photoshop files using appropriate tools and techniques.
Use an iterative design process to create professional-level digital artwork using Adobe Photoshop.
Assess design solutions and articulate their strengths and weaknesses.

rows.title: Visual Development for Animation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the various development processes involved in visual development for animation
Design and illustrate scenery for an animation or game
Conceptualize and illustrate original characters for animation
Create a storyboard based upon a script or narrative

rows.title: Digital Illustration II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Research a topic thoroughly for the purpose of creating an illustration.
Create a narrative sequence of illustrations.
Collaborate to generate concepts and realize them visually.
Conceptualize and produce characters for use in a narrative (animation, graphic novel, children's book).

rows.title: Internship/Work Experience 1
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Determine employment opportunities requiring entry-level skills in the visual media design profession
Obtain intership by sucessfully applying, interviewing and showcasing portfolio
Apply visual media design skills as required in a professional work environment
Manage effective communication with supervisors and co-workers

rows.title: Design Studio Practicum II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Lead group verbal critiques and give meaningful feedback to others.
Manage other students in complex design projects requiring multiple contributors.
Work independently on projects while meeting deadlines and developing relevant and meaningful design solutions.

rows.title: Home Health Aide
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Follow the agency protocol for infection control and utilize personal protective equipment in any patient care skill in a home based setting.
Identify the roles and responsibilities of a home health aide, including equipment to bring to patients home, safety and infection control in a home based setting.
Define applicable emergency procedures that could be used in a home setting.
Explain the difference between a home health aide and a CNA.
Perform patient care related to activities of daily living in a home based setting.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the historical background of nursing, including how the role of the LVN has evolved over time.

Analyze basic concepts in nursing, including legal and ethical issues, HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act), confidentiality, nursing process, communication skills, documentation, and patients’ rights.
Apply evidence-based practice in performing the necessary nursing interventions appropriate for the clients' condition.
Perform fundamental nursing skills and demonstrate various physical assessment techniques utilizing the appropriate plan of care according to findings.
Perform basic nursing skills and complete each procedure accurately, prioritizing nursing care based on appropriate clinical judgment and critical thinking skills.

rows.title: Clinical and Skills Lab I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and utilize the proper techniques of medical/surgical asepsis with patients, supplies, and equipment.
Apply critical thinking and appropriate clinical judgment when providing nursing care and monitoring patients' conditions.
Employ professional conduct, appearance, and cultural competency.
Identify changes in a client’s condition or assessment findings and report appropriately.
Communicate with the healthcare team and document nursing care, including basic assessment and administration of medications.

rows.title: Psychology in Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare historical and current perspectives on psychology related to nursing.
Explain the legal and ethical aspects of mental health nursing care, including client rights, confidentiality, and treatment appropriateness.
Determine how neuroscience relates to nursing care of clients with mental and psycho-physiological health challenges.
Provide professional and therapeutic communication in all aspects of the vocational nursing role.
Identify appropriate nursing responsibilities for clients suffering from stress, crisis, and abuse and determine the common defense and coping mechanisms.
Identify different types of mental, behavioral, mood, neurocognitive, and personality disorders, as well as nursing implications and appropriate treatments.

rows.title: Clinical and Skills Lab II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assemble the appropriate equipment and provide an accurate description of the purpose of each adult medical surgical skill performed.
Apply the current standards during the satisfactory performance of each adult medical surgical skill utilizing at least ten (10) of the LVN Department's Standard Steps of Nursing Procedures
Explain the nursing responsibilities before, during, and after each adult medical surgical skill is performed and formulate a patient teaching plan that includes its description and purpose.
Perform hands-on assessment and application of appropriate nursing interventions for clients with medical surgical disorders.
Apply nursing care and interventions to clients with medical surgical disorders, utilizing critical thinking and appropriate clinical judgment.

rows.title: Advanced Medical Surgical and Community Health Nursing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate between types and stages of shock, its potential complications, and appropriate nursing interventions utilizing reasonable clinical judgment and critical thinking.
Compare right- and left-sided heart failure, upper and lower airway disorders leading to respiratory failure and acute renal failure versus chronic renal failure.
Distinguish forms of cancer affecting gastrointestinal, hematological, lymphatic, neurological, and reproductive health and describe the implications for nursing in response to those distinct forms.
Describe the development of community health nursing, including the history of nursing elements of practice roles and functions.

Describe the LVN scope of practice established by the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT) and nursing responsibilities in home health settings, long-term care, rehabilitative nursing, and during disasters.

rows.title: Manufacturing Processes
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the operation and functions of basic machine shop tools.
Explain tolerances and their importance to part manufacture.
Assess and apply safe machine shop practices.
Perform metal cutting, threading, and surface hardening operations.
Describe metal coding and numbering systems.

rows.title: Our Stories
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Investigate creative storytelling and oral history research methods through the lens of intersectionality.
Examine creative storytelling as a transformative social, cultural, political, and historical practice.
Apply feminist theory to stories related to social, political, and economic issues.
Produce creative and ethnographic storytelling work informed by technical guidelines.

rows.title: Introduction to Masculinity Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss how sex, gender expression, and gender identity function within larger economic and political landscapes.
Analyze how masculinities and masculine roles are constructed and how constructs vary according to systems of difference.
Evaluate the impact of dominant forms of masculinity on public health and societal well-being.
Analyze key cultural works aimed at resisting dominant forms of masculinity within and across different racial and ethnic groups.
Evaluate the effectiveness of organizations and social movements aimed at constructing new masculinities, particularly in terms of impact on interpersonal violence and gender inequality.

rows.title: Ending Sexual Violence: Peer Education
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze major forms of power abuse in intimate relationships
Analyze the interaction between dominant culture stereotypes and false explanations for sexual violence
Evaluate the effectiveness of a local community based organization addressing the problem of sexual violence
Apply principles of peer education and feminist consciousness raising in the preparation of facilitation plans
Apply varied peer education methods in the facilitation of a presentation on sexual violence prevention
